Grandma Rosa's Sunday Gravy
Serves 8, about 3 1/2 hours
2 lb pork neck bones
1 lb Italian sausage
3 cans (28 oz) crushed tomatoes
6 cloves garlic, sliced
1/4 cup olive oil
1 tsp red pepper flakes
Brown the meat in the oil, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes. Simmer covered on low for 3 hours, stirring every 20 minutes.

Skillet Cornbread
Oven 425°F (220°C), 10-inch cast iron
1 1/2 cups cornmeal
1/2 cup all-purpose flour
1 tbsp sugar
2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt
1 1/2 cups buttermilk
2 large eggs

Stop 6: The Ashby Building (1911)
Completed in 1911 for a wholesale grocery firm, the eleven-story Ashby Building was among the first in the city to use a reinforced concrete frame. Its terra-cotta facade, with 1,240 cream-colored panels, was cleaned and restored in 2009 at a cost of $3.2 million.
Look up at the 10th floor to find carved grapevines and wheat sheaves, a nod to the original tenant. The ground-floor arcade now holds a bakery and a bike shop.
From here, walk two blocks north to Stop 7, about 4 minutes.

By the summer of 1886 the river wards held nearly 40,000 people, most of them packed into frame cottages built in a hurry and close together. Fire was a constant fear; the volunteer companies of the Fourth Ward answered 212 alarms that year alone.
The council's answer, an ordinance requiring brick party walls on all new construction, passed 17 to 9 in October 1887. Builders protested that it would raise the cost of a cottage from about $600 to $950.

Know Your Rights: Heat Season
From October 1 through May 31, landlords must keep indoor temperatures at least 68°F between 6 AM and 10 PM when it is below 55°F outside, and at least 62°F overnight whatever the outdoor temperature.
Hot water at a minimum of 120°F must be provided all year round.
If you have no heat, tell your landlord in writing first, then report it to the housing hotline at 555-0193. Keep a log of dates, times and indoor temperatures.

Walk-in flu clinics run Saturdays 9 AM to 1 PM through November 21. Most insurance plans cover the shot at no cost; without insurance it is $35.

Introduction
My grandmother cooked for eleven people every Sunday in a kitchen barely 6 feet wide, on the third floor of a building on Rowan Street that still stands. She never measured anything. When I finally stood beside her with a notebook in 1998, she was 84, and I wrote down "a handful" so many times that I started weighing her handfuls instead.

Delmont Park
Designed in 1894 and covering 218 acres, Delmont Park is the city's second-largest green space. The lagoon, about 0.8 miles around, is stocked with bluegill and largemouth bass; catch-and-release fishing is allowed with a state license.
The conservatory, rebuilt after a hailstorm in 2014, keeps its palm house at a steady 75°F all year. Admission is free, though a $10 donation is suggested.
Restrooms are open from 7 AM to 9 PM, April through October.

How to vote early
Early voting runs from Monday, October 19 through Sunday, November 1, 2026, at any of the city's 51 early voting sites. Hours are 9 AM to 7 PM on weekdays and 9 AM to 5 PM on weekends.
Bring a government-issued photo ID if you are registering at the same time. You may also request a mail ballot until October 29.
On Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, polls are open 6 AM to 7 PM and you must vote at your assigned precinct.

Riding the Metro with a bike
Bikes are allowed on all trains except during rush hours, 7:00 to 9:00 AM and 4:00 to 6:00 PM on weekdays. A maximum of 2 bikes is permitted per car, and you must use the first or last door.
Every city bus has a front rack that holds 3 bikes. Load from the curb side and tell the driver before you unload.
Folding bikes, when folded, are welcome at all times at no charge.

Eating in Tanner Square
The blocks around Tanner Square have the densest cluster of Ukrainian, Polish and Mexican bakeries in the city, many open by 6 AM. Expect to pay $3 to $4 for a pastry and about $12 for a full breakfast.
For dinner, the stretch of 18th Street between Corliss and Mercer has more than 30 restaurants within a 10-minute walk. Reservations are rarely needed on weeknights, but on Saturdays arrive before 7 PM or expect a wait of 45 minutes or more.
